main_body: Japanese merchant building (machiya) with tiled roof and two-story facade
top_band: blue-grey tiled roof ridge and slope from rows 1 to 30 (plus secondary awning slope at rows 41-46)
evidence: The building clearly shows a foreshortened top roof surface (rows 1-30) with individual tile courses and a ridge beam, an eave overhang shadow at row 31-32, an upper plaster wall with recessed lattice windows (rows 33-40), a lower tiled awning (rows 41-46), and a recessed ground-floor facade with wooden lattices, noren curtains, and dark entrance doorway (rows 48-77).

style.evidence: The roof tiles have a 5-step blue-grey ramp with per-tile highlights, and the plaster wall has subtle two-tone dithered grain. However, compared to the Beodeul reference buildings, the plaster lacks organic speckle, the wooden lattice and noren curtains are very repetitive/geometric, and the overall surface texture is slightly stiffer and more mechanical, though still well-shaded and properly constructed.
